newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Optus says still in pay-TV talks with Telstra.
newsitem.headline: Optus says still in pay-TV talks with Telstra.

text.p: Optus Communications Pty Ltd said on Monday that it was still in talks with fellow telecom group Telstra Corp about sharing infrastructure to deliver separate pay television services for both groups.
"There are on-going discussions between Optus and Telstra to see if there is room for infrastructure co-operation," Optus chief operating officer Ziggy Switkowski told reporters.
Both Optus and Telstra are spending jointly over A$7 billion rolling out separate cable systems which are to be used to carry telephony and pay television services.

"There are proposals that are on the table that are being considered, that have the potential to eliminate duplication for aerial cabling and to minimise on-going overbuilding of the network and to take a big step towards sorting out the pay-TV industry," Switskowski said.
Optus and Telstra confirmed last month they were in talks about forming a pay TV deal that would stem the huge losses both groups are experiencing from their respective pay-TV businesses.
"Those discussions are continuing between the companies and there are some commercial aspects that are separating us at the moment," Switkowski said.

Switkowski was answering questions after the official opening of the Jasuraus cable link from Australia to Indonesia in which both Optus and Telstra were partners along with PT Indonesian Satellite Corp (Indosat).
Telstra is a partner in the Foxtel pay-TV service with Rupert Murdoch's News Corp Ltd. Optus fully owns the Optus Vision cable network following a recent restructuring.
Analysts said Optus and Telstra would like to strike a pay-TV deal ahead of initial public offerings for both companies later this year.
